subject: MSA/Order Form — inspection boundaries, SOC 2 assertion mapping, and evidence cadence for MedNow pilot
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@mednow.com>, Ben Chang <ben.chang@mednow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MSA/Order Form — inspection boundaries, SOC 2 assertion mapping, and evidence cadence for MedNow pilot

Alexis / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our current redline of the MSA + Order Form and an evidence matrix that maps the SOC 2 assertions we usually surface to the artifacts customers request during onboarding. Key asks from our side so we can get this across the finish line: 

- Confirmation of the pen-test notice window you can accept for the pilot (we propose a 7 day standard, with an option for an expedited 72-hour window for urgent tests if pre-authorized).
- Clarify which systems are in-scope for your SOC 2 expectations (inference runtime, KV cache, telemetry pipeline, onboarding portal, other).
- Preferred sample set approach for staged evidence (sampling vs full artifacts) and a primary contact for log retention/forensics requests.

We're cc'ing Marissa (legal) and Karthik (infra) to capture constraints and propose language. If acceptable, I can drop a DocuSign link for the Order Form + short SOW and schedule a brief follow-up to confirm dates.

Attachments: redline_msa_v3.docx (docx, 42KB); evidence_matrix_mednow.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — inspection boundaries, SOC 2 assertion mapping, and evidence cadence for MedNow pilot

Internal notes / draft response for Alexis: 

Grace — quick legal take after a first pass on the redline:

- Inspection boundary: propose we limit "inspection" to environments defined in the Order Form (staging and production) and explicitly carve out ephemeral developer sandboxes and customer-managed integrations. This reduces scope creep.
- Pen-test notice: prefer 7 calendar days as standard. For urgent third-party vulnerability remediation we can accept a 72-hour expedited window but require a pre-approved researcher whitelist and a signed NDA amendment.
- Evidence cadence: recommend a standard SLA of 3 business days for routine artifact requests (e.g., control descriptions, configuration snapshots), and 1 business day for SOC 2 incident escalation requests.
- Data retention/logs: we will provide redacted aggregated telemetry for forensic requests; raw logs will require a legal intake and approved scope due to PII.
- Access model: ephemeral, time-boxed IAM roles with logging + single-use certificates for inspection; all access events logged to our audit trail.

Karthik — can you confirm the feasibility of 72-hour expedited access and single-use certs? Also, need a short description of what we can include in the evidence bundle (e.g., SOC 2 report (redacted), control matrix, sample log extracts, pen-test executive summary).

I'll draft a short paragraph to include in the Order Form (inspection/access procedures + escalation cadence). Once we have internal signoff I'll send to Alexis with a proposed pen-test window.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: legal_comment_summary.txt (txt, 4KB)

From: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@mednow.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Chang <ben.chang@mednow.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — inspection boundaries, SOC 2 assertion mapping, and evidence cadence for MedNow pilot

Hi Grace / Marissa —

Thanks for the draft and the matrix. A few things from MedNow's side: 

1) Pen-test notice: 7 days is fine as a default, but for our internal compliance we typically expect a 72-hour notice for third-party penetration tests as long as the scope is limited to non-customer-facing services. Would Redwood consider a two-track notice: 7 days for broad inspections; 72 hours for targeted tests limited to a pre-agreed asset list?

2) SOC 2 scope: we need the inference runtime, the customer-facing API gateway, and the telemetry pipeline (for alerting) to be explicitly listed as in-scope. Can you confirm whether KV cache contents may contain customer PII in any of your managed modes? If so, we need a stricter access model.

3) Evidence timing: for production-impacting incidents we require 24-hour initial acknowledgment and a 3 business day window for preliminary artifacts. For non-critical discovery requests we can accept 5 business days.

4) Regarding redactions — we appreciate redacted test reports/executive summaries. For forensic work we'll need a named contact and an evidence delivery mechanism (secure SFTP or signed AWS presigned objects).

We are targeting a pilot integration in March; if we can lock the Order Form and inspection language this week I'd like to propose a pen-test window March 7–11 (internal kickoff March 4).

Best —
Alexis Turner
Sr. Security Program Manager, MedNow
alexis.turner@mednow.com | +1 (617) 555-2210

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@mednow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — inspection boundaries, SOC 2 assertion mapping, and evidence cadence for MedNow pilot

Alexis —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level response and a proposed compromise: 

- Notice windows: we can accept the two-track model you proposed (7 days for broad inspections; 72 hours for targeted tests) provided the targeted tests are limited to a mutually agreed asset list and the researchers are pre-approved. We'll add language requiring a scope sheet before testing.
- KV cache and PII: Karthik confirms our managed KV cache is encrypted at rest and by default we mask PII in support artifacts; however, raw cache snapshots may contain ephemeral customer identifiers in some onboarding flows. We'll add a clause that raw cache extracts require a legal intake and additional redaction.
- Evidence timing: to align both sides, Redwood proposes: 24-hour incident ack, 3 business day preliminary artifact delivery for production-impacting items, and 5 business days for routine requests. We can add an "expedited" track for regulatory requests with a 1 business day SLA (requires pre-agreement).

Proposed immediate next steps: 
1) Marissa to update the redline to reflect the two-track pen-test notice and the evidence cadence table.
2) I will send a DocuSign link for the Order Form + pilot SOW once legal signs off.
3) If MedNow is comfortable, confirm the March 7–11 pen-test window now so we can reserve capacity.

HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7234/records/HB-2027-0412 (for internal reference)
DocuSign will be sent after legal approval.

Thanks —
Grace

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — inspection boundaries, SOC 2 assertion mapping, and evidence cadence for MedNow pilot

Finalized language for the Order Form (draft): 

- Inspection & Access: "Customer may request access to environments defined in Section 2 of the Order Form for the purposes of audit and inspection. Access shall be time-boxed and provided via ephemeral credentials; Redwood will log and retain all access events. Ephemeral access to raw production logs or cache extracts requires written intake and may be subject to redaction and a separate data-processing addendum."

- Penetration Testing: "Standard notice of seven (7) calendar days. For targeted tests limited to a mutually agreed asset list, Customer may provide seventy-two (72) hour notice. All tests must be executed by pre-approved researchers and follow the Target of Opportunity process in Appendix A."

- Evidence Cadence: table (stringified for the redline) — Request type / Acknowledgment SLA / Preliminary artifacts: 
  * Production-impacting incident / 24 hours / 3 business days
  * Routine discovery request / 3 business days / 5 business days
  * Regulatory expedited request / 1 business day / as agreed

- Deliverables: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), control matrix, pen-test executive summary (redacted), sample log extracts (redacted), and any additional artifacts as mutually agreed. Evidence delivery via secure presigned S3 links or secure SFTP.

I've attached the updated evidence matrix with the cadence table. Once Grace confirms MedNow accepts March 7–11 for the pilot pen test, I'll upload the redline to DocuSign and copy in MedNow's security contact.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence_matrix_mednow.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB)
